subject: Sample: a first-pass review tool, and what it would have to earn
preheader: Sample issue for the legal section. The products and the sponsor below are fictional.

lead.title: A first-pass review tool only pays if a lawyer still owns the file
lead.summary: This sample lead is about how a small practice would judge an AI contract tool. The product named later in the issue, ClauseHarbor, is not real. The point of the sample is the shape of the briefing: one lead, a few tools, a playbook, a short link list, and labeled sponsor slots.
lead.whyItMatters: A practice makes money on this category only when the tool shortens a first pass that a lawyer would have billed anyway, and when a human still checks the work before it reaches a client. If the check takes as long as the original review, the subscription is a cost, not a gain.

tools.name: ClauseHarbor
tools.summary: Fictional sample. A first-pass contract review desk that flags missing clauses and odd dates in a closed file.
tools.whyItMatters: Used on last year's closed matters, it can show whether a first pass gets shorter before anyone risks a live draft.
tools.pricing: Sample pricing, not a live offer.

tools.name: Docketline
tools.summary: Fictional sample. Intake questions and a conflict checklist for a new matter, before a person opens the file.
tools.whyItMatters: Cleaner intake means fewer unpaid hours spent chasing facts the client could have given on day one.
tools.pricing: Sample pricing, not a live offer.

tools.name: Precedent North
tools.summary: Fictional sample. Drafts a research memo outline from authorities the firm already trusts.
tools.whyItMatters: The gain is a faster outline, not a memo that goes out unsigned. The lawyer still writes the conclusion.
tools.pricing: Sample pricing, not a live offer.

playbook.title: How a 12-lawyer firm would trial a review tool
playbook.intro: This playbook is sample guidance for the format. It is not advice for any firm or any matter.
steps: Pick one matter type, not the whole practice.
Run the tool on closed files first.
Have a lawyer check every suggestion before it touches a live draft.
Track time saved against the subscription for two weeks.
Keep the tool only if the recovered time covers the cost twice over.
